title: The pesticide resistance treadmill
bottleneck: Pests evolve resistance to every major pesticide class, typically within a decade of introduction, forcing ever-higher doses and new chemistry — a treadmill the industry is losing as discovery of novel modes of action slows and regulatory costs rise. Broad-spectrum pesticides devastate beneficial insects and pollute ecosystems, while resistance management like refuges and rotation is widely ignored because it costs yield in the short term.
why_it_blocks: Losing effective pesticides removes the tools protecting a large share of global harvests, and no replacements are coming fast enough.
current_state: Resistance is documented in hundreds of pest species; biopesticides and RNAi sprays are promising but not replacements at scale. Resistance is documented in hundreds of pest species; biopesticides and RNAi sprays are not replacements at scale.
